summary: This benchmark evaluates the impact of unfreezing a 2,306-parameter modular router ('donated router') in convolutional and GRU host architectures on a synthetic register-routing task. Unfreezing yields a consistent 10.26–10.90 percentage point accuracy improvement over frozen baselines and slightly outperforms matched native pretraining. While the scope is limited to a synthetic micro-benchmark evaluated on two random draws, the experimental controls, intervention checks, and reporting of paired confidence intervals are rigorous.
strengths: Carefully isolated experimental design that changes exactly one training decision (freezing vs. unfreezing 2,306 weights) across identical host and router weight initializations.
Comprehensive mechanistic controls, including link-edit counterfactual evaluations and read-score shift ablations confirming router dependence.
Rigorous statistical reporting with paired 95% bootstrap confidence intervals across both architecture families and seeds.
Transparent documentation of execution parameters, hardware environment (Mac Studio CPU), wall-clock time, and memory footprint.
weaknesses: Evaluated exclusively on a small synthetic pointer-following task, leaving real-world transferability to large-scale transformer architectures or production routing unproven.
Limited sample size of only two host architectures and two random seed draws (503 and 607).
No verified external repository access was provided via the submission portal, limiting independent verification to the manuscript text.
suggestions: Extend the evaluation to standard transformer-based mixture-of-experts (MoE) or modular routing benchmarks to assess ecological validity.
Increase the number of random initializations and seed draws beyond two to demonstrate general statistical stability.
Provide public repository access directly linked through the submission platform for independent code audit and execution.

claims.text: Letting the original router adapt recovered 10.26–10.90 percentage points of held-out accuracy after 128 updates.
claims.source: Internal mathematical consistency check across Table 1 rows (69.74-58.84=10.90 pp, 69.18-58.59=10.59 pp, 73.76-63.17=10.59 pp, 73.52-63.26=10.26 pp)

claims.text: The adapted donor finished 0.20–0.38 points ahead of the matched-pretraining native router in both host architectures and both training draws.
claims.source: Internal consistency verification against Table 1 adapted minus native intervals: +0.38 pp [+0.27, +0.49] and +0.20 pp [+0.13, +0.27] for Convolution; +0.31 pp [+0.22, +0.40] and +0.23 pp [+0.15, +0.31] for GRU

claims.text: Shifting the adapted router's final read scores reduced clean accuracy to 0.48–0.73%, consistent with the adapted hosts continuing to rely on routing.
claims.source: Manuscript reported ablation controls; verified as internally plausible for score-permutation mechanistic disruption in routed networks
